# the contributor audit: power truncation and the dominant-normal cone

Full sources read:

* `candidate 888842a3bcf9aa99`
* `candidate c3c2ca0e4dcbdc9d`
* `candidate 8c5bbb9eb6411d6e`

The proofs pass, within their stated scope. The earlier archived moment
theorems were also read; these notes correctly identify truncation as
an application rather than a new independent moment theorem.

The beta-kernel identity for p>2 has coefficient p(p-1)(p-2)/2, and
both endpoint singularities in the normalized quadratic integral are
integrable. Comparing two truncation levels leaves exactly the stated
finite remainder; no differentiation under an improper integral is
used. The p=1 examples are exact and satisfy concavity.

For the nonsymmetric version, every strict superlevel block is an
interval containing the chosen peak. Its reciprocal side-length
coefficient is nondecreasing under truncation. The quadratic peak-index
moment inequality therefore retains that coefficient through positive
level integration, giving the all-real-p>=2 moment inequality. Direct
differentiation of the finite sum then proves the normalized truncation
law. The step-function knot integral and the c=R limiting bound handle
all repeated levels, zero endpoints, and peak plateaus.

For the directional cone, the conditional simplex law is derived with
Jacobian (1-W)^(d-1). Its conditional tail is a clipped dth power. The
assumed ratio makes its central value at most1/2. If neither threshold
crosses its lower endpoint, convexity of the positive-part power gives
the reflected-pair inequality; if one crosses, its full mass alone pays
the bound. Every pair attains equality at the single original tilt0.
The single-vertex determinant formula and its coefficient C_u are
correct. The subsequent truncation bound thus controls all tilts for
the stated continuous normal, not merely a zero-tilt cap.

The explicit cone constants are strictly below1 for every integer d>=2;
their algebra proves the ratio hypothesis and final Gamma_d/2 factor.
The remainder is positive. Through-point inclusion, vertical caps,
zero-radius fibers, and allowable continuous affine maps are accounted
for. The theorem deliberately leaves the other continuous normal
directions untreated and is not a general OC theorem.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
